Subject: Renewal planning — mid-contract growth and co-term question

Hi Sean,

We're planning Orchid's Q2 budget and looking at next steps for our Redwood contract. We've seen a 45% spike in inference volume since Dec (mostly embeddings + short-form generation). Renewal is due in June, but procurement wants to understand options if we increase committed capacity mid-term and how co-terming would work if we add a top-up now.

High-level asks:
- Can you share a path to add committed capacity mid-contract with minimal pro-rata penalty?
- What's your recommended co-term approach if we want everything to align to Jun 30 renewal?
- Any short-term credits or safeguards Redwood offers when growth is unexpected?

I attached a usage snapshot for Q4–Q1. Procurement will join future discussions: procurement@orchidhealth.com.

Thanks,
Maria

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — mid-contract growth and co-term question

Hey Maria — thanks for the snapshot, that's helpful. Quick notes below and I'd like to schedule 30 minutes to walk through a concrete proposal (I attached an initial draft).

Quick answers: 
- Mid-contract top-ups: we support a staged top-up with pro-rata billing, or an immediate committed increase. For smaller bumps (<50% of current commit) we typically offer a softened uplift (reduced surcharge) if the customer commits to the remainder of the contract term.
- Co-terming to Jun 30: we can apply an annualization option where added units are annualized to the co-term date rather than billed straight pro-rata. That reduces short-term invoice shock.
- Safeguard/credits: we can offer a one-time growth credit (typically expressed as a % of the top-up for the first month) and a temporary elevated burst allowance while the contract is amended.

Attached: Redwood_Safeguard_Proposal_v1.pdf — preliminary numbers and two paths: (A) staged top-up with month-1 credit OR (B) immediate commit with a smaller per-unit discount and full co-term annualization.

Can you do Thursday 2/16 at 10am PT for a quick alignment?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Orchid Health — renewal/top-up asks (need quick pricing guidance)

Ben / Naomi — forwarding Orchid's ask. Key points: they spiked ~45% and are considering a 2.5x committed increase. Renewal co-term is Jun 30. Procurement prefers quarter-end co-term.

Proposed play (my thinking):
1) Offer Path A (staged top-up): 6-month staged add (monthly billing), month-1 growth credit = 30% of top-up spend, unused credits do NOT roll forward — they convert to first-month offset at renewal reconciliation; co-term annualization applied at renewal for the added units.
2) Offer Path B (immediate commit): Convert to a midterm amendment, annualize to Jun 30, give 12% per-unit discount at 2.5x baseline and one-time 20% invoicing credit to offset migration setup.

Questions:
- Legal: any appetite to create a limited rollback if usage drops 30% vs forecast? (safeguard clause)
- Finance: do the month-1 credit mechanics and conversion at renewal look clean? We should propose a simple reconciliation: top-up units credited first, then new term commit reconciles remaining delta.

I need sign-off to present Path B as our preferred commercial if they want predictability.

—Sean

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@orchidhealth.com>, Ethan Reid <ethan.reid@orchidhealth.com>, procurement@orchidhealth.com

Subject: Orchid renewal — proposed safeguard plan & next steps

Hi Maria / Ethan / procurement team,

Great call — thanks for the time today. Per our discussion, here's the proposal we agreed to iterate on and next steps. I've attached an updated one-pager and included the core commercial terms below.

Summary (agreed options):
- Path chosen: Immediate commit with co-term annualization to Jun 30 (you indicated preference for predictability).
- Committed increase: 2.5x baseline units (commence 2/20/2028).
- Per-unit commercial: 12% per-unit discount vs list for the added units for remainder of current term (annualized to Jun 30).
- One-time setup & mitigation credit: 20% credit applied to the first invoice after amendment (to offset migration and spike).
- Safeguard: If observed usage in the 60-day window after commit drops >30% vs forecast, Orchid can request a single one-time partial rollback discussion; any rollback requires mutual agreement and will include a graceband adjustment over the next monthly invoice.
- Reconciliation at renewal: Amortized top-up units are reconciled against actual usage during the final 30 days of the term; any shortfall will be invoiced as true-up, any surplus converts into the new term's consumption bucket.
- SLA/support: No change to core SLA; we will temporarily elevate burst allowance by 25% for 60 days while traffic stabilizes.

Attachments: Redwood_Safeguard_Proposal_v1.pdf (updated) — contains sample invoices and amortization schedule.

Next steps:
1) Orchid to confirm acceptance of commercial (reply-all).
2) Redwood legal to prepare an amendment and updated SOW (Ben & Naomi will lead).
3) Procurement to provide PO or procurement timeline; Redwood finance to issue updated invoice after amendment executes.

If that summary matches what you heard, please reply to confirm and Ben/Naomi will start the amendment draft.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this in place quickly.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
